en-US.author: Viswajith M P
en-US.description: Zero-trust secrets engine that replaces dangerous .env files. AES-256 encrypted vaults, least-privilege tokens for CI/CD, and instant DEK rotation, without ever putting your master password on a runner.
en-US.longDescription: An encrypted vault for your API keys and secrets, because .env files have never once kept a secret.
en-US.name: envseal
en-US.releaseNotes:
New: file secrets, sealed alongside your env vars
envseal set KEY --file PATH seals any file up to 10 MB into the same vault as your environment variables — TLS certificates, service-account JSON, .p12 keystores, SSH keys, and kubeconfigs. --env-var sets the injected variable name and defaults to KEY.
# Seal a certificate and expose a private path to the app
envseal set TLS_CERT --file ./certs/server.pem --env-var TLS_CERT_PATH
# At runtime, $TLS_CERT_PATH points at a private temp copy
envseal run -- node server.js
# Need the file at a fixed path for a legacy tool?
envseal get TLS_CERT -o ./server.pem
At runtime, EnvSeal decrypts the file to a private temp path (0600, or 0700 if the source was executable on Unix), preserves its extension, and overwrites and deletes it when the process exits. Contents are zstd-compressed only when that makes them smaller.
list shows the binding in a terminal (TLS_CERT [file -> $TLS_CERT_PATH]), edit renders file entries read-only, and scoped CI tokens can include or exclude individual file keys. Use run or get for files; export and load remain text-only.
Also in this release
- list, get, export, and load now resolve the current branch's tag automatically when one exists, matching run — no --tag needed.
- remove refuses to guess when both base and a branch tag exist, and now requires --force in non-interactive mode.
- list verifies the vault signature before showing keys. Vault reads are capped at 64 MB, token payloads at 4 MB.
- git-setup surfaces failures instead of ignoring them, and safely merges the pre-commit guard with existing shell hooks.
No vault format changes or migration needed. Existing vaults keep working; the one behavior change is that scripts calling envseal remove without a TTY now need --force.
